$comment: WHERE THIS PACKAGE APPLIES. Replace all of it with your own region - this ships configured
for greater Hartford, Connecticut, because it is a region whose answer is already known, so
you can run a sweep and see what a correct result looks like before pointing it somewhere
`region` is the hard boundary. Anything the generator emits outside it is a build error.
That guard exists because a dropped minus sign on a longitude looks completely normal and
puts a beacon in western China.
name: Greater Hartford, CT
$search_areas_comment: Boxes that `python -m tools.sweep` searches for structures. Each must sit inside `region`.
Declaring several small areas rather than one big one is usually what you want: a sweep of
a whole metropolitan region returns every chimney on every apartment block, and you pay for
each one in objects. Narrow boxes around the places that actually carry tall structures -
a ridge line, an industrial flat, a downtown core - give a far better package.
Remove this block entirely to sweep the whole `region` box instead.

metacomet_ridge.$comment: The trap ridge west of Hartford: Avon Mountain at the south end, north over Talcott Mountain into Simsbury. Carries the broadcast antenna farm that serves the Hartford market - masts of 300-500 ft standing on a 900-1000 ft crest, so their beacons sit at 1300-1500 ft MSL and are the first thing you see approaching the valley from the west at night.

south_meadows.$comment: The industrial flats between I-91 and the Connecticut River, north of Hartford-Brainard. Covers the generating station stacks, which read as separate lights in a short line on a night circuit.

reference_point.$comment: Map centre, and the origin for preview output. Old State House, downtown Hartford.
